newsitem.title: HONG KONG: "Euro" bond benchmark still an open question - EC.
newsitem.headline: "Euro" bond benchmark still an open question - EC.

text.p: The question of which European government bond will be the benchmark for bonds denominated in the euro remains open, Paul Goldschmidt, director of Financial Operations Services at the European Commission, said Wednesday.
"It is still an open question. We expect the market will determine one or several benchmarks," Goldschmidt told bankers at a forum on European Monetary Union sponsored by HSBC Markets.
He said French government bonds are likely contenders because of France's sophisticated market infrastructure and its commitment to redenominating French bonds into euros.
Goldschmidt said German bunds would also be in the running as a benchmark for euro Eurobonds.
Italy priced its one billion seven-year euro Eurobond launched in March against the 6.00 percent OAT due in 2004.
Italy's euro Eurobond, the first issue of its kind for a sovereign, will make payments in ecu until European monetary union becomes effective.
The euro will become Europe's single currency starting on January 1, 1999.
"It also might be the European Investment Bank, which is a major issuer," he said.
Goldschmidt was in Hong Kong with European Commission Director of Monetary Affairs Herve Carre to explain the impact of European monetary union on financial markets to Asian investors.
